newsitem.title: HONG KONG: China insurer buys stake in Beijing Oriental Plaza.
newsitem.headline: China insurer buys stake in Beijing Oriental Plaza.

text.p: The People's Insurance Company of China has taken a 15 percent interest in the Oriental Plaza property development in Beijing, one of the project's joint venture partners said on Wednesday.
A spokeswoman for Orient Overseas (International) Ltd (OOIL) said the interest of existing shareholders, including OOIL and Cheung Kong (Holdings) Ltd, was diluted following the deal.
"Our equity interest (after the deal) is 23 percent of the 85 percent," the OOIL spokeswoman said.
Cheung Kong officials were not available for comment. Relevant officials at People's Insurance in Beijing also could not be contacted.
Local newspapers reported on Wednesday that the Chinese insurer took the 15 percent stake for US$225 million.

Oriental Plaza is a development of about six million square feet of office, hotel, residential and retail spaces in Beijing. OOIL held about 23 percent of the project and Cheung Kong group about 64 percent before the deal with People's Insurance.
